methodological_rigor.justification: The study combines TCGA-derived bioinformatics (LASSO-Cox development of a 10-gene FRG signature) with in vitro validation in two cell lines (CAL27, UPCI-SCC-090) and IHC on 179 retrospective samples. Validation is internal only (random partitioning into training/testing/combined subsets from the same TCGA-HNSC cohort); authors explicitly acknowledge no external cohort could be found. In vitro validation is limited to single HPV-negative and HPV-positive cell lines with no in vivo work. Statistical approach (unpaired t-test, one-way ANOVA with Tukey, Cox regression, time-ROC, KM) is appropriate but no multiplicity correction is described across numerous bioinformatic comparisons, and no power calculation is reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is a retrospective bioinformatic prognostic model derivation with preclinical cell-line mechanistic validation, equivalent to case-series / low-quality cohort level of evidence (Oxford 4) since much of the evidence rests on cell-line experiments and TCGA retrospective data. Clinical relevance is plausible: TRIB3 is proposed as a ferroptosis-linked therapeutic target and a nomogram is built for prognostication. However, the translational path is not demonstrated; no prospective validation or clinical decision-making impact is shown.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prognostic prediction-model paper, TRIPOD is the relevant standard. The manuscript reports predictor selection (LASSO), calibration curve, time-dependent ROC with AUCs, DCA and a nomogram, which addresses many TRIPOD items, but key items are missing or underreported: handling of missing data, full model equation with intercept, sample-size justification, and external validation. TCGA and GSE83519 are publicly available data sources (redacted URLs) so the analytic data is in principle reproducible; cell-line and IHC protocols are described in detail, but no analysis code is shared. Data availability is thus intermediate.

novelty_literature.justification: Ferroptosis-related gene signatures for HNSCC have been previously published (e.g., references 31, 32, 60 in this manuscript), so the core concept of an FRG prognostic model is incremental. The novel elements are the explicit stratification by HPV status (HPV-negative-specific model) and the mechanistic demonstration that TRIB3 modulates ferroptosis markers (Fe2+, GSH, MDA, ROS) in both HPV-negative and HPV-positive HNSCC cells. This constitutes a meaningful extension rather than a field-defining advance.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable, with clearly labeled methods subsections and a logical results flow from bioinformatics through cell biology to IHC. Some passages are verbose or awkward (e.g., circular definitions around CIBERSORT scores summing to 1, repetitive discussion paragraphs) and several sentences are overlong. Figures are referenced systematically, and tables/supplementary materials are cited appropriately, but the text would benefit from tightening and clearer delineation between discovery and validation claims.

key_strengths: Combines TCGA bioinformatics with cell-line functional validation (siRNA knockdown, overexpression, TEM, Fe2+/GSH/MDA/ROS assays) and IHC on 179 retrospective cases
HPV-status-stratified analysis addresses a genuine biological distinction with prognostic implications
Appropriate modelling pipeline (LASSO-Cox, time-ROC, calibration, DCA, nomogram) for a prognostic signature
key_concerns: No external validation cohort; authors acknowledge GEO datasets lacked HPV annotation and relied solely on internal TCGA partitioning
In vitro validation limited to a single cell line per HPV subtype and no in vivo data
Mechanism by which TRIB3 regulates ferroptosis is not dissected (no pathway experiments beyond ferroptosis markers)
Incremental novelty: several prior FRG signatures for HNSCC already exist; additional value comes mainly from HPV stratification and TRIB3 functional data
Reporting gaps relative to TRIPOD (missing data handling, sample-size justification, code availability)
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent but incremental retrospective bioinformatic prognostic model with limited mechanistic and no external/in vivo validation; plausibly acceptable at a mid-tier specialty oncology journal after major revisions addressing validation and mechanism.
